$comment: The fixed evaluation set required by spec §11.1, over two documents.
`eval-terms-ja.pdf` is generated by `npm run fixtures:sample` and is deliberately NOT a
document any heuristic was fitted to — segmentation, the fragment rules, the batch size and the
§7 thresholds were all settled against sample-contract-ja.pdf and bitcoin.pdf. Measuring quality
on those would report the fit, not the quality.
`bitcoin.pdf` is the opposite case and is here for a different reason: the segmentation was
tuned on it, but these eighteen queries were written by an outside reviewer against the paper's
own sections, not by whoever wrote the code. They caught a real defect on the first run — two
pages whose figures outnumbered their prose were being split line by line, so every answer came
back cut mid-sentence. Queries someone else wrote are worth more than queries that fit.
Expectations name a passage by a distinctive snippet rather than by segment ID. Segment IDs
depend on the segmentation heuristics, so a frozen set keyed on them would silently break -
or silently pass against the wrong passage - the moment those heuristics are tuned. The
harness matches snippets with the same normalization exact search uses.
Every `status_not` query asks about something genuinely absent from its document, so a
`matched` result is a false positive rather than a gap in this file.
